jobs.title: Senior Customer Success Manager - French Speaking
jobs.description:
Industry leader? Well, how about an industry creator?!

WalkMe, an SAP company, pioneered the world's leading Digital Adoption Platform, helping organizations navigate change across any application or system. Today it is the platform that drives AI adoption across the enterprise. Enterprise work stays fragmented across applications, and that fragmentation compounds as AI advances. Traditional training and vendor-provided help leave organizations managing change one application at a time. WalkMe guides people through change, brings AI into the flow of work, automates tasks and shows executives how workflows perform. Global leaders including IBM, Nestlé, Thermo Fisher Scientific, and the U.S. federal government trust WalkMe. WalkMe turns AI potential into AI performance.

So, if you’re an expert in your field, and looking for an opportunity to work, collaborate, and innovate with some of the most talented people out there, WalkMe is the place for you!

We’re looking for a French speaking
Customer Success Manager, Commercially adept but with a technical curiosity in the Product and what it can do for our Customers, to help take digital adoption and WalkMe to the next level.

As a Customer Success Manager, you’ll be responsible for being a trusted advisor to a portfolio of around 10 Fortune 1000 WalkMe customers, helping them achieve maximum value from the WalkMe platform. You will understand your clients' digital adoption goals, and recommend technology solutions to help them get the most out of our product and meet/exceed their goals. You will report to the Manager of Customer Success.

What You'll Own

Be the 'voice of the customer' and provide internal feedback to maximize customer value and retention

Schedule and prepare Executive Business Reviews for customers, with the top priority of increasing customer adoption and proving Return on Investment that leads to renewals/expansion

Maintain an understanding of our product and roadmap, so you can guide customers to success and continue to promote up their Adoption Score

Educate customers on the most relevant features of their specific requirements

Understand your customer's industry trends, challenges with digital adoption, and current and potential use cases for WalkMe

Establish and develop strategic, trusted advisor relationships at the highest relevant levels (Decision Makers, Champions, Economic Buyers) by guiding the customer on best practice usage of the platform to help manage risk and meet/exceed their goals

Work with the internal Account team and Customer to develop a Success Plan outlining how WalkMe addresses their immediate/future needs (including metrics for success)

Monitor customer health to reach out to customers before risks escalate and identify remediation options

Partner with WalkMe Account Team (Renewal Managers, Account Executives, Services, Technical Account Managers) to ensure that customers renew and expand

What You'll Need to Succeed

5+ years of customer advocacy and engagement experience in Enterprise SaaS customer success, account management, or post-sales relationship management working with Fortune 1000 companies and their executives

Experience managing a quarterly retention and growth quota

You've maintained a book of Enterprise customer accounts (4000+ Employees)

Increase customer satisfaction, adoption, and retention applying to a technical product

High competency in sales discovery methodologies and an ability to run Return on Investment discussions and have some experience in an enterprise solution sales environment, having partnered with account executives to develop and close sales opportunities

Fluent in both English and French is a must

jobs.description:
UK CITIZENSHIP REQUIRED FOR THIS POSITION: Yes

RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: No relocation assistance available

TRAVEL: Yes, 25% of the Time

Regulatory Compliance Analyst

Location:
Remote with travel to central London 1-2 times a month

Clearance:
SC (or eligible)

Salary:
£40,000 - £50,000

What's your possible?

At Northrop Grumman UK, you are part of a team driving innovation where it matters most, solving tomorrow's challenges and shaping the technology solutions of the future. We call it Defining Possible.

This mindset goes beyond our customer solutions. It is the foundation for your career development, the way we support one another, and the positive impact we make across our communities.

This is more than just a job. It's a mission.

As a Regulatory Compliance Analyst, you will play a highly visible role at the heart of our international privacy and data protection programme. Working across Northrop Grumman UK's International Holdings, you will help shape, implement and continuously improve our privacy governance framework, ensuring compliance with UK GDPR, EU GDPR and emerging international privacy regulations.

This is a unique opportunity to influence strategic decision-making across multiple countries and functions while helping the organisation manage privacy risks in a practical and business-focused way. You will work closely with Legal, HR, Security, Compliance, IT and business leaders, acting as a trusted advisor and helping to embed privacy by design throughout the organisation.

Joining a collaborative and globally connected team, you will have the opportunity to work on complex challenges, support international initiatives, and help foster a strong culture of privacy and accountability across the business.

What You'll Do

Support and enhance the privacy governance framework across Northrop Grumman UK's international operations.
Translate privacy legislation and regulatory requirements into practical policies, standards, controls and business processes.
Provide expert advice and guidance on privacy obligations, compliance risks and data protection best practice.
Conduct privacy risk assessments, supplier due diligence reviews and Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs).
Review and support Data Processing Agreements, data sharing arrangements and international data transfer mechanisms.
Deliver privacy awareness initiatives, engagement activities and training programmes that strengthen organisational understanding and accountability.
Collaborate with global privacy, legal, compliance and business stakeholders to support business priorities while maintaining strong privacy governance.
Monitor developments in privacy legislation and recommend actions that ensure ongoing compliance and effective risk management.

What We're Looking For

Essential Skills and Experience

Strong knowledge of UK GDPR, EU GDPR and wider privacy and data protection principles.
Experience working within privacy, governance, compliance, risk, legal or data protection functions.
Demonstrable experience translating regulatory requirements into practical business controls and governance processes.
Experience conducting privacy risk assessments, DPIAs and third-party privacy reviews.
Excellent stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence and advise colleagues at all levels.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capability with exceptional attention to detail.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, changing and internationally diverse environment.

Desirable Experience

Experience supporting multinational organisations operating across UK and European jurisdictions.
Knowledge of international data transfer requirements and cross-border privacy governance.
Experience supporting employee representative bodies or Works Council consultations.
Professional privacy, compliance or data protection qualifications.

We know that everyone brings different experiences and strengths. If you're excited about this opportunity but don't meet every requirement, we'd still love to hear from you.

Security Clearance

Due to the nature of our work, you must be a UK national and able to gain and maintain UK Government security clearance in line with the job role and requirements.

Our recruitment team is on hand to answer any questions and will guide you through the process: talentenquiries@uk.ngc.com

Benefits

As well as working on meaningful projects that help protect national interests and deliver real-world impact, you'll have access to a comprehensive benefits package, including:

Flexible working options, including hybrid working arrangements
Compressed fortnight working pattern with every other Friday off
Private medical insurance, dental cover, life assurance and competitive pension scheme
Flexible benefits package including critical illness cover and health cash plan
Holiday buy and sell scheme
Annual performance incentive programme
Career development and learning opportunities
Employee wellbeing initiatives and support programmes

Why Join Us?

A Mission to Believe In

Every day we contribute to building a more secure and connected world. Whether supporting critical national capabilities, advancing technology innovation or protecting sensitive information, your work will have genuine purpose and impact. You can also find community and belonging through our employee networks and STEM volunteering opportunities.

A Place to Belong and Thrive

At Northrop Grumman UK, every voice matters. We value different perspectives, experiences and backgrounds because they help us create better outcomes for our customers, colleagues and communities.

At Northrop Grumman UK, you are part of a team driving innovation where it matters most, solving tomorrow's challenges and shaping the technology solutions of the future. We call it Defining Possible.

This mindset goes beyond our customer solutions. It is the foundation for your career development, the way we support one another, and the positive impact we make across our communities.

This is more than just a job. It's a mission.

As a Regulatory Compliance Analyst, you will play a highly visible role at the heart of our international privacy and data protection programme. Working across Northrop Grumman UK's International Holdings, you will help shape, implement and continuously improve our privacy governance framework, ensuring compliance with UK GDPR, EU GDPR and emerging international privacy regulations.

This is a unique opportunity to influence strategic decision-making across multiple countries and functions while helping the organisation manage privacy risks in a practical and business-focused way. You will work closely with Legal, HR, Security, Compliance, IT and business leaders, acting as a trusted advisor and helping to embed privacy by design throughout the organisation.

Translate privacy legislation and regulatory requirements into practical policies, standards, controls and business processes.
Provide expert advice and guidance on privacy obligations, compliance risks and data protection best practice.
Conduct privacy risk assessments, supplier due diligence reviews and Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs).
Review and support Data Processing Agreements, data sharing arrangements and international data transfer mechanisms.
Deliver privacy awareness initiatives, engagement activities and training programmes that strengthen organisational understanding and accountability.
Collaborate with global privacy, legal, compliance and business stakeholders to support business priorities while maintaining strong privacy governance.
Monitor developments in privacy legislation and recommend actions that ensure ongoing compliance and effective risk management.

Essential Skills and Experience

Strong knowledge of UK GDPR, EU GDPR and wider privacy and data protection principles.
Experience working within privacy, governance, compliance, risk, legal or data protection functions.
Demonstrable experience translating regulatory requirements into practical business controls and governance processes.
Experience conducting privacy risk assessments, DPIAs and third-party privacy reviews.
Excellent stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence and advise colleagues at all levels.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capability with exceptional attention to detail.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, changing and internationally diverse environment.

Desirable Experience

Experience supporting multinational organisations operating across UK and European jurisdictions.
Knowledge of international data transfer requirements and cross-border privacy governance.
Experience supporting employee representative bodies or Works Council consultations.
Professional privacy, compliance or data protection qualifications.

At Boeing, we innovate and collaborate to make the world a better place. We’re committed to fostering an environment for every teammate that’s welcoming, respectful and inclusive, with great opportunity for professional growth. Find your future with us.

Boeing Global Services (BGS) is looking for an Experienced or Senior Supply Chain Compliance Analyst – Self Governance and Compliance
to join our team in Dallas, TX.

Our teams are currently hiring a broad range of experience levels including Experienced & Senior Supply Chain Compliance Analyst.

Position Responsibilities
:

Support Boeing Global Services Supply Chain Government’s compliance team in strengthening supply chain compliance processes and training across operations.
Partner with cross-functional teams to support compliance procedures, training curriculum development, and process adherence.
Assist in monitoring internal compliance activities, identifying risks, and helping drive corrective actions.
Contribute to the continuous improvement of compliance programs, processes, documentation, and employee learning initiatives.
Collaborate with stakeholders to ensure policies, procedures, and training materials are practical, current, and aligned with Boeing standards.
Applicable and appropriate educational/certification credentials from an accredited institution and/or equivalent experience is required.

Basic Qualifications (Required Skills/Experience):

1+ years of experience in project management and/or cross-functional integration
Experience supporting the creation and presenting of training materials
3+ years of experience in Supply Chain processes
Strong communication skills, Strong problem solving skills, and Strong drive for process improvement

Preferred Qualifications (Desired Skills/Experience):

Ability to coach and support supply chain employees effectively
Ability to interpret policies, procedures, and regulatory or contractual requirements
Direct experience with Boeing and/or Boeing Global Services supply chain operations
Experience developing or delivering compliance training and utilizing training development technologies
Familiarity with supplier management, audits, assessments, risk identification, and corrective action management
Strong understanding of continuous improvement, change management, and documentation control
Experience using Boeing systems, tools, or internal process frameworks
Knowledge of BGS Supply Chain command media, policies, procedures and work instructions

Conflict of Interest:

Successful candidates for this job must satisfy the Company’s Conflict of Interest (COI) assessment process.

new_jobs.title: Lead Trade Compliance Analyst
new_jobs.description:
MANTECH
seeks motivated, career and customer-oriented Lead Trade Compliance Analyst
to join our team. This is a Remote
opportunity.

Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To

Manages the development, implementation, and oversight of corporate and program wide International Trade Compliance Frameworks.
Authorize export and import compliance protocols, validate International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and Export Administration Regulations (EAR) licensing strategies, and implement governance structures to ensure total alignment with Federal Customs and Border Protection regulations.
Orchestrates regulatory compliance operations, customs clearances, and international transport authorizations across the USPACOM AOR to support distributed logistics networks.
Manage complex technical data packages, validate export licenses, and oversee Host Nation customs permit processing at Theater Joint Distribution Center nodes.
Direct internal compliance audits and lead the resolution of international trade, ITAR, or border discrepancies with Mission Partners and customs authorities.
Provides leadership, guidance, and mentoring to subordinate staff.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in International Business, Logistics, Supply Chain Management, or a related field and 12+ years of position-relevant experience.
Professional certification in Trade Compliance (e.g., Certified ITAR Professional [CIP] or Certified Export Specialist [CES]).

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in related discipline.
Experience managing export/import control regimes for USSOCOM or USPACOM programs.
Extensive familiarity with Automated Commercial Environment (ACE) and international Status of Forces Agreements (SOFA).

Clearance Requirements

Must be a US citizen with ability to obtain a fully adjudicated Secret clearance after starting.

Physical Requirements

The person in this position must be able to remain in a stationary position 50% of the time.
Occasionally move about inside the office to access file cabinets, office machinery, or to communicate with co-workers, management, and customers, via email, phone, and or virtual communication, which may involve delivering presentations.
